text:
Marta: Quick RFC followup — I sketched an "autonomous fallback operator" concept for canary/A-B. TL;DR: a lightweight control-loop that negotiates degrade policies with runtime, observable via Console. Wanted to surface tradeoffs.

Sam: love it. do you mean this lives in control-plane or a sidecar near the router?

Marta: sidecar-adjacent. idea: small operator per-cluster that maintains soft-state and issues low-latency fallback commands to the router. Control-plane can push high-level intent (budget, sensitivity) and operator translates to local decisions.

Jia: unclear on split-brain. if control-plane loses contact, how does operator avoid aggressive global rollbacks?

Marta: good point — operator must prefer safe-allowlist vs aggressive-swap. proposal: two-tier policy: (1) local probe-driven degrade thresholds, (2) centrally-specified must-not-exceed constraints. If control-plane unreachable, operator falls back to last-good constraints and applies conservative ramp-down.

Leo: what signals do we need? latency p95, error-rate, model-confidence? also cost signals for Dedicated vs Hosted.

Marta: minimal set: p50/p95 latency, request errors, per-tenant quality regression signal (from evals), and probe success rate. cost considered offline — operator can tag routes with cost hints but cost-driven autoswitch remains admin action.

Sam: API surface between control-plane and operator?

Marta: rough proto sketch:
```
POST /v1/operators/{id}/intent
{
  "policy_id": "canary-123",
  "budget_qps": 200,
  "degrade_mode": "soft|hard",
  "max_swap_pct": 15,
  "safety_window_s": 300
}
```
Operator exposes local telemetry and accepts probe hooks: `/v1/operator/{id}/probe-result` with small batched events.

Jia: operator->router contract?

Marta: simple command set: `route_split(route, percent)` `pause_route(route)` `force_fallback(route, variant)` and `observe(route, metrics)`. Keep it minimal to avoid coupling. Router enforces per-tenant caps.

Leo: are we storing state? if operator restarts, we need idempotence.

Marta: state machine persisted to local disk and reconciled with control-plane. Intent objects are versioned; operator only acts on increasing intent revision. On startup it replays last intent and re-evaluates probes before changing traffic.

OpsBot: deploy-bot: canary/operator v0.1 deployed to staging 10:30AM :rocket:

Sam: tradeoffs I see:
- Pros: low-latency decisions, reduces SLO blips during control-plane jitter
- Cons: more distributed decisioners -> harder global reasoning, potential policy divergence

Marta: mitigation ideas: deterministic conflict resolution (higher-priority constraint wins), policy linting in control-plane, and telemetry that surfaces when local operator deviates from intent.

Jia: testing plan?

Marta: staged plan:
1) unit tests for operator state machine
2) end-to-end in staging with canary traffic mirrored
3) chaos test: control-plane partitioned
4) runbook updates for oncall (fast manual override via Console)

Leo: rollout safety: add a `safety_window_s` (as in proto) and `rollback_budget` to limit how many forced fallbacks per hour.

Marta: agree. also add `probe_backoff` — if probes are noisy don't flip frequently.

Sam: interface boundary note: do not expose model-specific logic (e.g., logits) to operator. operator works on high-level metrics only.

Jia: we should add an eval hook to the Canaries pipeline so quality regressions can signal operator.

Marta: noted. next steps: I'll draft a short RFC with the proto + state machine and include the sample probe schema. Can someone own the RFC review? @Sam @Jia

Sam: I can take first pass this week.

Jia: I'll review and add probe schemas.

Marta: thanks — scheduling a 30m sync Friday 9:30am. If you have objections reply here, else I'll create RFC doc and link.

Leo: :thumbsup:

Sam: thanks, nice synthesis.

Marta: linking the staging deployment logs after sync. Thanks all.
